title: Production acceptance: publish and deploy the exact verified release
evidence_required: FT-003-AC-001 — RED: after dependency closure and the local gate, fresh read-only production comparison is expected to show that production checkout HEAD and installed version do not yet both equal the newly gated full commit; if a safe rerun finds the exact commit already installed and healthy, RED_NOT_APPLICABLE because manufacturing absence would require an unauthorized downgrade or service disruption, and alternative proof is preserved pre-implementation GREEN followed by the same ordered no-broader-mutation revalidation. GREEN: one time-ordered redacted receipt chain proves the gated tree stayed unchanged; an ordinary clean commit was pushed without force and the configured GitHub ref resolved to its full ID; the actual access route was resolved from current read-only evidence; fresh preflight found exactly one healthy systemd somonwatch.service identity with no competitor; the clean production checkout advanced only by safe fast-forward to that ID; target build, linkage, embedded version and redacted produced-binary doctor passed before runtime mutation; only somonwatch.service was stopped, installed and started; installed version, active health, restart count and scoped logs passed. Decisive comparison: local HEAD, GitHub ref, production HEAD, target-built version and installed version converge on one full commit while ordered receipts show every stop boundary and no runtime mutation before target proof. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-004-T3-FT-003-W2/TASK-004-T3-FT-003-W2-acceptance-evidence.md.

FT-003-AC-002 / REQ-008 — RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: deliberately deleting/replacing/migrating SQLite, changing settings, or disturbing an unrelated workload to observe claim absence would violate the accepted production-safety claim; alternative proof: use read-only before/after identity, integrity and host comparisons around the one scoped watcher update. GREEN: stopped pre-install and post-start receipts prove the same SQLite path/file identity, successful read-only integrity check, equal non-secret settings digest, and post seen_ads count not below the stable pre-install count; redacted stable comparisons prove unrelated containers/services, failed units, sockets, firewall, routes and SELinux unchanged, with no secret or raw host inventory disclosed. Decisive comparison: settings digest equality, nondecreasing seen count, stable database identity, and equal unrelated-host fingerprints/statuses permit differences only in the watcher checkout/build/install artifacts, process and somonwatch.service lifecycle. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-004-T3-FT-003-W2/TASK-004-T3-FT-003-W2-acceptance-evidence.md.
purpose: Deliver the completed local feature set to production through one exact, state-preserving and host-isolated systemd release with auditable redacted evidence.
success_outcome: The locally gated commit is the exact commit on the configured GitHub ref, production checkout, target-built binary and installed binary; exactly one healthy somonwatch.service is updated, its settings/SQLite survive, and unrelated host state remains unchanged.
anti_goals: Do not reimplement or adopt acceptance proof owned by the three local implementation dependencies.
Do not add a deployment abstraction, script, CI/CD layer, alternative runtime, container route, migration, compatibility mechanism, package transaction, or infrastructure change.
Do not force-push, rewrite refs/history, reset, stash, discard, overwrite, or commit unrelated/unattributed local or production work.
Do not delete, replace, migrate, repair, reset, or intentionally mutate the watcher database or settings.
Do not act on any container or unrelated service, process, socket, firewall, route, reverse proxy, SELinux setting/policy, package, database, or host configuration.
Do not expose Telegram tokens, environment contents, raw production inventory, access endpoints, or other secrets in commands, logs, receipts, Git, or chat.
Do not infer that the operator phrase sh igorprod is executable authority or that historical systemd evidence is current.

forbidden_scope: local production-source edits after the repository-native release gate starts
local Git history/ref rewrite, force push, deletion, or publication of unrelated/unattributed work
any production checkout other than the one bound by fresh evidence to the accepted watcher service and pushed commit
production Git reset, stash, force, discarded local work, non-fast-forward update, or ref rewrite
any production runtime other than one healthy host systemd somonwatch.service
all production containers and all unrelated services, processes, sockets, firewall, routes, reverse proxy, SELinux policy/mode, packages, databases, and host configuration
database content/schema mutation, migration, deletion, replacement, reset, or repair
environment-file content changes or any secret-bearing output/evidence
FT-001/FT-002 implementation or proof scope owned by dependency tasks
stop_conditions: Any dependency is not done or done_for_prod, its required verification is incomplete, or the current Planning Revision 1 task plans are not approved.
The local release gate fails, changes the gated source tree, or the intended commit contains an unexplained, unrelated, secret-bearing, or unattributed worktree change.
The configured publication target is not the intended GitHub repository/ref, a normal non-force push fails, or the remote ref does not resolve to the exact full commit ID.

Fresh read-only local discovery cannot reconcile the operator phrase sh igorprod with one authorized actual access command; an alias, script, host, user, privilege route, or target remains missing, conflicting, or ambiguous.

Fresh production preflight is not fully read-only before the first write or finds an unhealthy host, an unhealthy/absent/ambiguous/non-systemd watcher, more than one watcher process/runtime, any competing watcher container, or inconsistent checkout/unit/process/executable/user/environment/database paths.

The identified production checkout is dirty, diverged, ahead of the intended commit, cannot fast-forward exactly, requires force/reset/stash/discard, or does not equal the full commit after synchronization.
The target scripts/build.sh gate, linkage, embedded commit/version, or redacted produced-binary service-user doctor fails; the installed runtime must remain unchanged.
SQLite cannot be inspected read-only, integrity/path/file identity is uncertain, or stable pre-install settings digest and seen_ads count cannot be captured after stopping only somonwatch.service.

The existing installer would modify anything outside watcher-owned install/backup paths and somonwatch.service metadata/lifecycle, would alter environment contents or database state, or requires a user/group/runtime migration.

Stopping, installing, starting, or checking only somonwatch.service fails, or recovery would require an improvised rollback, database replacement, container action, unrelated-service action, rapid restart pressure, or broader host mutation.
Postflight installed commit, unit health/restart count, redacted doctor, scoped logs, settings digest, seen_ads non-loss, database identity, or unrelated-host comparison fails or is inconclusive.
Any command or evidence path would expose a token, environment contents, access endpoint, raw host inventory, or other secret.

Execution reveals an unresolved permission, runtime, production checkout, state authority, tier, dependency, proof, or task-boundary decision, or requires a project path outside the hard write boundary apart from workflow-owned evidence/lifecycle bookkeeping.

constraints: Preserve the exact order: closed local dependencies and ./scripts/build.sh; ordinary clean commit and non-force GitHub push with exact remote-ref match; freshly resolved access command; fresh read-only production identity/health/state/host preflight; safe exact-commit fast-forward synchronization; target scripts/build.sh plus linkage/version and redacted produced-binary doctor; stop/install/start only somonwatch.service; installed-version, health, restart, log, state and host-isolation postflight.

Before any production connection, resolve the actual authorized access command read-only from current shell/command/SSH evidence; neither sh igorprod nor prior SSH-alias diagnostics may be assumed, executed, or recorded unredacted without unambiguous confirmation.

Continue past preflight only for one healthy existing host systemd somonwatch.service consistently bound to one process, executable, service user, environment path, SQLite/debug paths and production checkout, with no competitor and healthy unrelated workloads.

Production Git may fetch and fast-forward only the identified clean watcher checkout to the already-pushed exact commit; no force, reset, stash, checkout overwrite, discarded work, merge commit, alternate ref, or other checkout is allowed.
Run the target-compatible build and redacted produced-binary doctor before stopping the installed service; a failure makes no runtime/install change.

After stopping only somonwatch.service, capture stable database/settings evidence, invoke only the existing scoped install route, and start only the same unit; keep the environment file, SQLite database and debug directory in place.
Receipts must be time-ordered and redacted, prove every decisive comparison, and omit tokens, environment values, access endpoints and raw host inventory.

The local non-empty write boundary is hard. External writes are limited to the exact GitHub ref, identified watcher checkout/build, watcher-owned installer targets/backups and somonwatch.service lifecycle; all other external state is forbidden.
invariants: All three implementation dependencies are closed before local release verification, and their acceptance proof remains owned by those tasks.
One full commit ID is identical at local HEAD, configured GitHub ref, synchronized production HEAD, target-built version and installed version.
No production write occurs before a fresh healthy unambiguous systemd-only watcher identity and unrelated-host preflight; historical evidence is insufficient.
The production checkout is advanced only by a clean exact fast-forward with no force/reset/stash/discard, and target build/doctor passes before installed-runtime mutation.
Only somonwatch.service and watcher-owned checkout/build/install artifacts may change; no container or unrelated host/service/network/security/database state changes.
The existing environment, SQLite and debug paths remain in place; settings digest is unchanged and seen_ads loses no stable pre-install rows.
Secrets and raw production inventory never enter Git, chat, command echo, logs, or acceptance receipts.
A retry begins again with access resolution and fresh read-only preflight; ambiguity or failure stops instead of broadening authority or improvising recovery.
verification_targets: FT-003-AC-001: one ordered redacted receipt chain proves dependency closure, local ./scripts/build.sh, unchanged gated tree, full release commit, exact configured GitHub ref, freshly resolved access route, single healthy systemd identity, no competing watcher, clean exact fast-forward production sync, target gate/linkage/version/redacted doctor before runtime mutation, only somonwatch.service stop/install/start, and passing installed-version/unit/restart/log postflight.

FT-003-AC-002 / REQ-008: read-only preflight, stopped stable-state and post-start observations prove SQLite integrity and file identity, equal non-secret settings digest, nondecreasing seen_ads count, and unchanged redacted fingerprints/statuses for unrelated containers/services, failed units, sockets, firewall, routes and SELinux.

T3 wrong-target and overwrite safety: receipts show how the actual access route, checkout, unit, process, executable, user, environment and database paths were cross-bound before first write; show a clean ancestry/fast-forward decision and exact post-sync HEAD; and show that every ambiguity, dirty/diverged state and non-systemd/container branch is a stop rather than an executed alternative.

T3 rerun and disclosure safety: a retry restarts from read-only discovery/preflight, pre-existing exact healthy deployment uses pre-implementation GREEN without manufactured downgrade, target build/doctor failure leaves the installed runtime unchanged, and stored evidence is redacted of secrets, access endpoints and raw host inventory.
